Interlocutors on Jammu and Kashmir 
 *201. SHRIMATI SHOBHANA BHARTIA: Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS 
be pleased to state: 
 (a) whether the three member team of interlocutors on Jammu and 
Kashmir appointed by the Centre has recently asked everyone, including 
separatists, to come and join talks with them; 
 (b) if so, whether the separatists in the valley are against 
holding any discussions with the interlocutors; 
 (c) whether the interlocutors have also expressed that the Kashmir 
issue cannot be resolved without involving Pakistan; 
 (d) if so, the reaction of Government in this regard; and 
 (e) the details of recommendations made by the three member team 
of interlocutors to Government and Government’s response thereon? 
 THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIR S  
(SHRI AJAY MAKEN): (a) and (b) A three member team of Interlocutors, 
namely,  
Dr. Dileep Padgaonkar, Prof. M.M. Ansari and Prof. Radha Kumar has 

 2 
been appointed to held a sustained dialogue with all sections of the 
people in Jammu and Kashmir. In this regard, during 

 3 
their visits to the State, they have made public their intention to 
give access to all groups of people including the separatists of meet 
them in this regard. Some separatists have made a statement in the 
media against holding discussions with the interlocutors. 
 (c) to (e) There are press reports about the interlocutors having 
stated that a comprehensive solution could not come without involving 
Pakistan. In this regard the stated policy of the Government is that, 
it is committed to discussing all outstanding issues with Pakistan, 
including the issues of Jammu and Kashmir, through a bilateral 
dialogue. The first Report of the Interlocutors has been received on 
01.11.2010. 
Providing access to Indian security agencies to 
encrypted messages of Blackberry 
 †*202. SHRI SATYAVRAT CHATURVEDI: Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS 
be pleased to state: 
 (a) whether it is a fact that the time -limit for the Blackberry 
handset manufacturing Canadian company ‘Research in Motion’, to 
provide access to the Indian security agencies to its messenger and 
enterprise services has again been extended up 31 December, 2010; 
 (b) whether it is also a fact that the encrypted (code language) 
messages of Blackberry cannot be read by the security agencies while 
being sent; 
 (c) the time when the Blackberry was first asked to provide access 
to Indian security agencies to its messenger and enterprise services 
and how many times the time-limit has been extended so far; and 
 (d) the reasons therefor? 
 THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE M INISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS  
(SHRI AJAY MAKEN): (a) to (d) Department of Telecommunications (DoT) 
on  
11th December, 2007, directed all the service providers not to connect 
or provide/run Blackberry e- mail and mobile messenger services unless 
the required moni toring system to the satisfaction of the security 
agencies are in place. Discussions were commenced with ‘Research in 
Motion’ (RIM), provider of the Blackberry services, as a result of 
which Voice, SMS and individual e-mail were made available to security 
agencies in readable format. Again, on 13th August, 2010, all the 
telecom service providers were instructed by the Department of 

 4 
Telecommunications to ensure that a technical solution for 
interception and monitoring of Blackberry services in readable format 
is made available to the law enforcing agencies by 31st August, 2010. 
In case no solution is provided then these services may be blocked as 
per the relevant clauses of the license in the interest of national 
security. RIM agreed to provide a solution for Blackberry messenger 
chat service for which upgradation of telecom service network was 
required. Telecom service providers were asked to upgrade their 
network by 22.9.2010. The telecom service providers have upgraded 
their network and the solution offered is being tested by the law 
enforcement agencies for which the time limit has been extended upto 
31.12.2010. RIM has assured that they will  

 5 
provide the final solution for lawful interception of BBM services 
31st January, 2011. With respect to security solutions for the 
Blackberry Enterprises Services, mutual consultations are on between 
the RIM and the Government and as such more time is required to 
achieve a closure. 
Inclusion of NRIs in Census data 
 *203. SHRI K.N. BALAGOPAL: Will the Minister of HOME A FFAIRS be 
pleased to  
state: 
 (a) by when the current Census process will be completed; 
 (b) whether NRI data will be included in the Census data; 
 (c) whether Government has received any request or proposal to 
include NRI data in the Census data; 
 (d) if so, the details thereof; and 
 (e) what action has been taken on the request? 
 THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS  
(SHRI AJAY MAKEN): (a) The Census Operations are conducted in two 
phases. The first phase of Census 2011 — Houselisting and  Housing 
Census commenced from  
1st April, 2010 and was completed in most parts of the country on 30th 
September, 2010. Only in the State of Chhattisgarh a time extension 
was given upto 31st October, 2010. The second phase of Census called 
“Population Enumeration” will be conducted from 9th February to 28th 
February, 2011 with a revisional round from 1st March to 5th March, 
2011. In certain areas which are inaccessible in February on account 
of heavy snow fall, the Population Enumeration was taken up in advance 
from 11th September, 2010 to 30th September, 2010 with a revisional 
round from 1st October, 2010 to 5th October, 2010. The data collection 
will be followed by data processing and dissemination of data 
thereafter. 
 (b) The following will be enumerated in the Population Enumeration 
phase:— 
 (i) All those who normally reside and are present in that 
household during the entire period of enumeration, i.e. from 
9th February to 28th February, 2011 (both days inclusive); 
 (ii) Those who are known to be normall y residing and had actually 
stayed during a part of the enumeration period in the 
household (9th February to 28th February, 2011) but are not 

 6 
present at the time of visit of the enumerator; 
 (iii) Those who are known to be normally residing in the 
household and are not present at the time of visit of the 
enumerator but expected to return by 28th February, 2011;  
and 
 (iv) Visitors who are present in the household censused by the 
enumerator and expected to be away from the place(s) of their 
normal residence during the entire enumeration period. For the 
purpose of enumeration such visitors will be treated as normal  

 7 
residents of the household where they are actually found 
during the enumeration period provided they have not been 
enumerated elsewhere. 
 If any NRI is present in the country, who satisfies the condition 
as above, he/she will be enumerated during Census exercise. However, 
NRIs who are not resident in the country and do not satisfy the 
criteria listed above, will not be enumerated in the Census exercise. 
 (c) to (e) Yes, representations were received from the World 
Malayalee Council Inc., New Jersey, USA and Overseas Indian Cultural 
Congress Coordination Committee, Kuwait for inclusion of NRIs in the 
enumeration process of Census. Replies have been given to them on the 
above lines.

Share of India in trade of handicraft items 
 *205. SHRI AVTAR SINGH KARIMPURI: Will the Minister of TEXTILES be  
pleased to  
state: 
 (a) the place and share of India in the total trade of handicraft 
items in the world; 
 (b) whether the share of India in the handicraft items in the 
world is less as compared to the ratio of handicraft items produced in 
the country; 
 (c) if so, the reasons therefor; and 
 (d) the steps taken by Government to increase the export of 
handicraft items? 
 THE MINISTER OF TEXTILES (SHRI DAYANIDHI MARAN): (a) As reported by 
Export Promotion Councils, India ranks No. 1 in case of Exports of 
hand made carpets with a share of 29% of the world trade. In respect 
of handicrafts items (other than hand made carpets) India ranks 7th 
amongst the exporting countries and share of India’s exports in world 
trade in handicrafts is approximately 2%. 
 (b) No, Sir, Approximately 75% of hand made carpets produced in 
India are being exported and 50% of handicraft items (other than hand 
made carpets) produced in India are being exported, as per reports of 
National Council of Applied Economic Research and Export Promot ion 
councils. 
 (c) Does not arise. 
 (d) The steps taken by Government to increase the exports of 
handicraft items include: participations in fairs/exhibitions abroad; 
thematic display and live demonstration of handicrafts in exhibitions 
abroad; organizing buyer-seller meets in India and abroad; brand image 
promotion of Indian handicrafts abroad through seminars and publicity, 
awareness programmes about technology, packaging and export policies 
in India to exporters; organizing Indian Handicrafts and Gifts F airs, 
product specific shows and Made in India show at New Delhi, providing 
assistance under Marketing Development Assistance and Market Access 
Initiative Schemes of Ministry of Commerce to exporter members. 
 Government has included all handicraft items under focus product 
scheme by allowing Duty Credit Scrip of 5% on FOB value of exports. 
Besides, an additional benefit of 2% of bonus over and above the 

 10 
existing benefit of 5% is also given. 2% interest subvention on Pre -
shipment and Post shipment export credit has also been extended. 
Rise in labour disputes in Andhra Pradesh 
 *206. SHRIMATI T. RATNA BAI: Will the Minister of LABOUR AND 
EMPLOYMENT be pleased to state: 
 (a) whether Government is aware that labour disputes are on the 
rise especially in the scheduled areas in Andhra Pradesh and other 
States; 

 11 
 (b) if so, the State -wise details thereof, during the last five 
years; and 
 (c) the steps being taken to provide speedy justice in labour 
disputes? 
 THE MINISTER OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT (SHRI MALLIKARJUN K HARGE): 
(a) and (b) Data on industrial disputes raised in the State sphere is 
not maintained Centrally. For the industrial disputes in the Central 
sphere, data is maintained as per the territorial jurisdiction of the 
Deputy Chief Labour Commissioner (Central)/Regional Labour 
Commissioner (Central). Similarly, data on industrial disputes arising 
in the Central sphere in the scheduled areas in the States is not 
maintained separately. Region-wise information of industrial disputes 
raised in the Central sphere before the Conciliation Officer notified 
for this purpose under the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, during the 
last five years is given in the Statement- I (See  below). No 
significant increase in industrial disputes in the Central sphere has 
been observed for the country as a whole is given in the Statement -II 
(See below).  
 (c) With a view of reduce industrial disputes, the conciliation 
officers notified under the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 try to 
resolve the disputes by holding conciliation proceedings w ith unions 
and the management. For speedy disposal of industrial disputes in the 
Central Government Industrial Tribunal -cum-Labour Courts (CGIT- cum-
LCs), a Scheme of Holding of Lok Adalats as an “Alternative Grievance 
Redressal Mechanism”  is being implemen ted. The Industrial Disputes 
Act, 1947, has recently been amended to set up a Grievance Redressal 
Machinery in every industrial establishment employing twenty or more 
workmen for speedy resolution of disputes arising out of individual 
grievances.

Completion of Hyderabad-Warangal NH by NHDP 
 *208. SHRIMATI GUNDU SUDHARANI: Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT 
AND HIGHWAYS be pleased to state: 
 (a) when was the Hyderabad -Warangal National Highway taken up by 
National Highways Development Projects (NHDP); 
 (b) whether it is a fact that the Highway was completed only up to 
Ghatkesar and the remaining stretch is yet to be completed; 

 19 
 (c) if so, the present status of this project; 
 (d) the reasons for delay in completing the project; and 

 20 
 (e) by when the remaining stretch is going to be completed? 
 THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS (SHRI KAMAL NATH): (a) 
to (e) The Hyderabd -Warangal section of NH -202 is being developed 
under NHDP in two phases i.e. Hyderabad-Yadgiri and Yadgiri-Warangal. 
 Under NHDP Phase-III, Hyderabad-Yadgiri stretch is being developed 
on DBFOT (Toll) basis and the concession agreement has been signed on 
24.2.2010. Between Hyderabad and Yadgiri, Hyderabad -Ghatkesar section 
is already 4-laned. The work is scheduled to be completed by December, 
2012. 
 The Yadgiri- Warangal stretch has been included for development 
under NHDP Phase-IVB, which is yet to be approved by the Government. 
It is too early to indicate the completion schedule. 
CGDA recommendation to ban DGDE 
 *209. SHRI K.E. ISMAIL: Will the Min ister of DEFENCE be pleased to 
state: 
 (a) whether it is a fact that the Comptroller General of Defence 
Accounts (CGDA) has asked the Ministry to ban the Directorate General 
of Defence Estates (DGDE), the custodian of all defence lands in the 
country, for widespread irregularities in the department and its 
failure to manage huge land bank in possession of the services and to 
transfer all defence estates to DRDO and MoD; and 
 (b) if so, the details thereof and Government’s reaction thereto? 
 THE MINISTER OF DEFENCE (SHRI A.K. ANTONY): (a) and (b) Controller 
General of Defence Accounts assigned Controller of Defence Accounts 
(Internal Audit) to carry out a special performance audit for examine 
the existing land acquisition system in order to identify bottlenec ks 
that account for delay and to suggest systemic measures to be taken to 
ensure that the Government does not end up incurring avoidable 
expenditure on account of interest on belated period of decretal 
amounts. The study report has been received. A number of 
recommendations have been made which inter alia mentioned that:— 
 (i) Service Headquarters and other user agencies like Defence 
Research and Development Organisation (DRDO), Ordnance 
Factories etc., may be authorized to deal directly with State 
Government authorities without intermediation of Directorate 
General of Defence Estates for acquisition of land, to 
expedite the land acquisition process. Elimination of the 
additional layer of Directorate General of Defence Estates 
from defence land acquisition p rocess shall speed up the 

 21 
acquisition process and is expected to eliminate time and cost 
over-runs both for land and infrastructure on this. 
 (ii) Keeping in view the very limited utility of the Directorate 
General of Defence Estates organisation, Ministry  of Defence 
may like to order a comprehensive study for disbanding this 
organisation from most of the activities from defence land 
management in a phased manner. 

 22 
 The report is under examination.

five schemes all over the country including the States of Uttar 
Pradesh, Bihar and West Bengal for enhancing production productivity 
and efficiency of the handloom sector and to enhance the income and 
socio-economic status of the weavers through skill upgradation and

  This scheme provides need based inputs to a “Cluster” of 300-
500 Handloom or a “Group” of 10-100 weavers for making them 
self-sustainable by providing them financial assistance for 
margin money, working capital, new looms and accessories, 
skill upgradation, marketing opportunities and for 
construction of workshed.

  This comprises of two separate schemes viz. the Health 
Insurance Scheme (HIS) for providing Health Insurance to the 
Handloom weavers and Mahatma Gandhi Bunkar Bima Yojana (MGBBY) 
for providing Life Insurance Cover in case of 
natural/accidental death, total/partial disability due to 
accident. 
 • Marketing and Export Promotion Scheme (MEPS) 
  This scheme provides marketing opportunities and 
infrastructure support through design development and 

 29 
marketing linkages to assist in the sale of the Handloom 
products both in domestic and international market.

  The scheme makes available all types of yarn at Mill Gate 
Price to the eligible  handloom agencies to facilitate regular 
supply of basic raw material of the handloom weavers and to 
optimize their employment potential. 

 30 
 • Diversified Handloom Development Scheme 
  This scheme provides assistance for technological and skill 
upgradation of weavers for design and product development 
through 25 Weavers’ Service Centres and 05 Indian Institutes 
of Handloom Technology all over the country to improve the 
productivity and earnings of the handloom weavers.

4 Mega Handloom Clusters at Sivasagar (Assam), Varanasi (Uttar 
Pradesh) Virudhunagar (Tamil Nadu) and Murshidabad (West 
Bengal) with a maximum project cost of Rs. 70.00 crore each 
for overall and holistic development of weavers of these 
areas.

(a) to (c) Review/updation of labour laws is a continuous process in

While undertaking such changes overall interests of labour 
†Original notice of the question was received in Hindi. 

 32 
like wages, employment, social, working environment, health and safety 
etc. are  
protected keeping in view the requirements of the Indian Industry to 
make it efficient and internationally competit ive. The required 
changes in the labour laws are accomplished by the Government after 
detailed consultation with the stake holders with a view to harmonize

 Accordingly in the recent past, a new law, namely, the Unorganized 
Workers’ Social Security Act, 2008 has been enacted. The salient 
features of the Act include formulation of welfare schemes for 
different sections of the unorganized sector workers on matters 
relating to life and disability cover, health and maternity benefits, 
old age p rotection etc. Besides, amendments have been carried out in 
the Payment of Wages Act, 1936 enhancing the wage ceiling from Rs.

10,000/- per month through notification; in the Payment of Bonus Act, 
1965 enhancing the calculation ceiling from Rs. 2,500/- to Rs. 3,500/-

covering contract workers engaged in construction activities; in the 
Apprentices Act, 1961 providing for reservation for Other Backward 
Classes; in the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961 increasing the medical 
bonus from Rs. 250/-  to Rs. 1,000/ - and also empowering the Central 
Government to increase it from time to time before very three years, 
by way of notification in th e Official Gazette, subject to maximum of 
Rs. 20,000/-; in the Workmen’s Compensation Act, 1923 by changing its 
name to the Employees’ Compensation Act, 1923 to make it gender 
natural and enhancing the compensation under the Act from Rs. 80,000/- 
to Rs. 1. 20 lakh in  
case of death, from Rs. 90,000/-  to Rs. 1.40 lakh in case of 
disablement, from  
Rs. 2,500/- to Rs. 5,000/- towards funeral expenses and increasing the 
wage ceiling limit for working out compensation from Rs. 4,000/ - to 
Rs. 8,000/- per month; in the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972 to cover 
teachers in educational institutions and to  
enhance the ceiling on gratuity from Rs. 3.5 lakh to Rs. 10 lakh; in 
the Employee’ State Insurance Act, 1948 to improve the quality of 
service under the scheme and als o to enable ESI infrastructure to be 
used to provide health care to workers in the unorganized sector; in 
the Plantations Labour Act, 1951 to provide safety and occupational 
health care to plantation workers and in the Industrial Disputes Act, 
1947 to ampl ify the term ‘appropriate Government’, enhance the wage 
ceiling from Rs. 1,600/ - to Rs. 10,000/- to cover workmen working in 

 33 
supervising capacity, provide direct access for the workman to the 
Labour Court or Tribunal, expand the scope of qualifications of 
Presiding Officers of Labour Courts or Tribunals, establish Grievance 
Redressal Machinery and empowering the Labour Court or Tribunal to 
execute the awards etc. 
 In the process, the labour laws have become simple, effective and 
beneficial for labour.

Strengthening disaster management mechanism in States 
†1604. SHRI JAI PRAKASH: Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be 
pleased to state: 
†Original notice of the question was received in Hindi. 

 108 
(a) whether the Central Government is providing help to States for 
strengthening efficient and active disaster management mechanism; and 
(b) if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS  
(SHRI MULLAPPALLY RAMACHANDRAN ): (a) and (b) Yes, Sir. The Central 
Government has undertaken various measures to help/assist the 
States/Union Territories (UTs) for strengthening the existing 
institutions and/or creating new such institutions for efficient 
management of disasters such as:— 
• Strengthening the States/UTs in preparation of Plans for 
Disaster Management in the State through National Disaster 
Management Authority (NDMA). An amount of Rs. 3.20 crore has 
been given by NDMA to different States/UTs during financial 
year 2009-10. 
• Issuing National Policy on Disaster Management and disaster 
specific and thematic guidelines for guidance of States/UTs in 
tackling disasters. NDMA has released 26 guidelines such as 
Management of Earthquakes; Landslides and Snow Avalanches; 
Chemical Disasters; Biological Disaster; Medical Preparedness 
and Mass Casualty Management etc. 
• Constitution of National Disaster Response Fund/State Disaster 
Response Fund for providing relief during disasters. Based on 
the recommendations of  
13th Finance Commission, corpus of Fund to the tune of Rs. 
33580.93 crore for State Disaster Response Fund has been 
earmarked for the period 2010 -11 to 2014- 15. During 2010- 11, 
Rs. 2948.795 crore has been released to the States as central 
share to State Disaster Response Fund (Calamity Relief Fund). 
• For Strengthening and Capacity Building measures of States, 
various steps have been taken up, viz.: 
(i) On recommendations of 13th Finance Commission, Rs. 525 
crore has been allocated for the States as Grant for 
Capacity Building for Disaster Response for the period 
2010-11 to 2014-15. The guidelines to this effect as well 
as  
Rs. 105 crore has been released to the States during 
2010-11. 
(ii) Programme for “ Institutional Strengthening and Capacity 

 109 
Building for Disaster Risk Reduction” under Government of 
India – “UNDP Disaster Risk Reduction Programme (2009-12)” 
is under implementation. 
(iii) Providing financial assistance to Administrative 
Training In stitutes and other training institutes in 
States/UTs for operation of a Faculty/  
Centre of Disaster Management for strengthening the 
Capacity Building measures of States/UTs through National 
Institute of Disaster Management (NIDM). 

 110 
(iv) Under the earlier conducted National Programme for 
Capacity Building of Engineers in Earthquake Risk 
Management (NPCBEERM) and the National Programme for 
Capacity Building or Architects in Earthquake Risk 
Management (NPCBAERM) with the objective to equip the 
working engineers and architects with relevant knowledge 
on the subject, till March, 2010, 2528 practising 
engineers and 1361 practising architects have been 
trained. 
(v) National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) is imparting 
training to various stakeholders including the training 
for the State Police Force employed for Disaster 
Management and sensitizing the community for Disaster 
preparedness. 
• Revamping of Civil Defence and Strengthening of Fire and 
Emergency Services in the States/UTs at a cost of Rs. 100 
crore and Rs. 200 crore respectively are under implementation.

†1605. SHRI KALRAJ MISHRA: Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be 
pleased to  
state: 
(a) whether Union Government has evaluated or is in the process of 
evaluating damages to khari f crop and loss of property and lives 
caused by heavy rains during monsoon this year in the State of Uttar 
Pradesh; and 
(b) the details of financial assistance being give to 
farmers/rural families? 
THE MINISTER OF STAT E IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS  
(SHRI MULLAPPALLY RAMACHANDRAN): (a) and (b) Yes, Sir. On receipt of a 
memorandum from the Government of Uttar Pradesh, seeking financial 
assistance for floods of 2010, an Inter -Ministerial Central Team 
(IMCT) visited the affected areas for an on- the-spot 
assessment/evaluation of the damage and requirement of funds for 
relief operations by  
State Government. IMCT visited the State from 19- 21 October, 2010 and 
again from  

 111 
29th October, 2010 to 1st November, 2010. The report of the Central 
Team will be considered by the Inter -Ministerial Group (IMG) and 
thereafter by High Level Committee (HLC) for assistance from National 
Disaster Response Fund (NDRF), as per the laid down procedure. 
The State Government concerned is primarily responsible for 
undertaking relief m easures at ground level in the wake of notified 
natural calamities, out of the corpus of State Disaster Response Fund 
(SDRF), in accordance with items and norms approved by the Government 
of India. In cases of calamities of severe nature, SDRF is 
supplemented by the National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF) in 
accordance with the laid down procedure.

 112

houses, (v) medical aid, (v) loss of utensils/clothing, etc.

385.39 crore in the State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF) for the year 
2010-11, comprising Rs. 289.04 crore as Central share and Rs. 96.35 
crore as State share. The 1st installment of the Central share of SDRF 
amounting to Rs. 144.52 crore was released, on 30th June, 2010. 
Keeping in view the severity of floods, the Government of India has 
also released Central Share of second installment of the same amount 
i.e. Rs. 144.52 crore, in advance, on 24th September, 2010, otherwise 
due to be release in December, 2010.

has considerably improved and is under control. The level of violence 
against the Security Forces have considerably reduced and is being 
closely monitored.

been killed in various incidents of law and order involved by SFs and 
the civilians. The State Government has sanctioned ex-gratia relief of

(b) Question does not arise. 
(c) The Population Census is an independent exercise and has n o 
connection with the BPL Census. While the former is conducted every 
decade by the Office of the Registrar General, India, Ministry of Home 
Affairs, the latter is the subject matter of Ministry of Rural 
Development. The Ministry of Rural Development provides financial and 
technical support to States/UTs for conducting the BPL Census 
generally in the beginning of the Five Year Plan, to identify the 
Rural Households living Below the Poverty Line who could be assisted 
under its various programmes. Last such Census was conducted in 2002 
for the Tenth Five Year Plan Period. First BPL Census was conducted in 
1992 for Eight Five Year Plan and the second in 1997 for Ninth Five 
Year Plan. The BPL Censuses conducted so far were actually conducted 
by respective States/UTs and had no links with Population Censuses. 
For conducting the BPL Census for the Eleventh Five Year Plan, the 
Ministry of Rural Development on 12th August, 2008 constituted and 
Expert Group to advice on the suitable methodology for identification 
of BPL households. The Expert Group under Chairmanship of Dr. N.C. 
Saxena submitted its report on 21st August, 2009. The report of the 
Expert Group was circulated among the State Governments/UT 
administrations and the concerned Central Ministries for their 
comments. The Ministry has also consulted various experts on the 
issue. Based on their suggestions a pilot survey is being conducted in 

 126 
254 villages to arrive at the methodology for the forthcoming BPL 
Census. In addition to the pilot survey  
through conventional questionnaire method, Participatory Rural 
Appraisal (PRA) technique is also being conducted in the same 254 
villages where household survey is conducted to corroborate the 
information received through the pilot surveys. Methodology for the 
BPL  
Census will be finalized by the Ministry of Rural Development on the 
basis of outcome of pilot survey and taking in to account the 
suggestions/ comments of States/UTs Central Ministries and experts.

Compensations to flood affected Haryana 
†1617. SHRI RANBIR SINGH PARJAPATI: Will the Minister of HOME 
AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) the details of the schemes for flood affected areas; 
(b) the amount of compensation provided by Government to flood 
affected Haryana State; 
(c) whether this amount should directly be deposited in bank 
accounts of the flood affected farmers so that these farmers get the 
entire amount; and 

 148 
(d) whether Government has any plan to divert flood waters to 
drought areas and if so, the details of that plan? 
†Original notice of the question was received in Hindi. 

 149 
THE MINISTER OF STAT E IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS  
(SHRI MULLAPPALLY RAMACHANDRAN): (a) The Schemes for flood control are 
planned, funded and executed by the State Governments concerned. The 
role of the Central Government is of a technical, catalytic and 
promotional nature. The Central Government has initiated various 
measures for assisting the States in the management of floods. 
During Eleventh Plan, “Flood Management Programme ” a State sector 
scheme amounting to Rs. 8000 crore under Central Plan proposed by 
Ministry of Water Resources has been approved ‘in principle’ by the 
Government of India on 02.11.2007. The scheme aims to provide central 
assistance to the State Governments/UTs for river management, flood 
control, anti- erosion works, anti -sea-erosion works, drainage 
development, flood proofing, flood prone area development programme, 
restoration of damaged flood management works, etc. in critical 
reaches which have secured all mandatory clearances. 
(b) and (c) The financial assistance from the relief fund in the 
wake of identified natural calamities including floods is provided, 
towards relief and not compensation of loss. The main objective of the 
said fund is to assist the affected farmers/persons to start their 
economic activities again and by way of gratuitous assistance as an 
immediate help to overcome the stress and not for compensation of 
loss. 
The primarily responsibility for undertaking rescue and relief 
measures in the event of  
natural disasters rests with the State Government concerned. The 
Central Government supplements the efforts of the State Governments by 
providing appropriate financial and logistic support. 
Financial support is provided in the form of State Disaster 
Response Fund (SDRF) constituted for each State, with certain 
allocated amount based on the recommendations of Finance Commission. 
In cases of calamities of severe nature, SDRF is supplemented by the 
National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF) in accordance with the laid 
down procedure. 
The State Government concerned, is required to incur the 
expenditure on relief operations of immediate nature, in conformity 

 150 
with the items & norms of assistance approved by the Government of 
India. 
The State of Haryana has been allocated an amount of Rs. 192.90 
crore in the State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF) account for the year 
2010-11, comprising  
Rs. 144.68 crore as Central share and Rs. 48.22 crore as State share. 
The 1st installment of the Central share of SDRF amounting to Rs. 
72.34 crore was released, on 30th June, 2010. The second installment 
of the same amount is due to be released in December subject to 
submission of utilisation certificate and annual report. 

 151 
(d) With regard to diversion of flood waters to drought areas, the 
Ministry of Water Resources (MoWR), which is the concerned Ministry, 
has informed that they have formulated a National Perspective Plan 
(NPP) for Wate r Resources Development in 1980 envisaging inter- basin 
transfer of water form surplus basins to deficit basins/areas which 
comprises of two components, viz. ; (i) Himalayan Rivers Development 
Component and (ii) Peninsular Rivers Development Component. National 
Water Development Agency (NWDA) was set up under the Ministry of Water 
Resources in 1982 for carrying out various technical studies to 
establish the feasibility of the proposals of NPP and to give concrete 
shape to it. Based on various studies conducted, NWDA has identified 
30 links (16 under Peninsular component and 14 under Himalayan 
Component) and received 36 proposals of Inter- State links from 6 
States for transfer of water from surplus basin to deficit basin. 
Tracking down remittances of NGOs 
1618. SHRIMATI SHOBHANA BHARTIA: Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government has asked the Intelligence Bureau to 
prepare a negative list of Non -Governmental Organisations (NGOs) and 
individuals to track down their sources of remittances; 
(b) if so, the reasons therefor and the details thereof; 
(c) whether there is growing evidence of the contravention of the 
Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA) in recent years; and 
(d) the steps Government plans to take to address future 
violation? 
THE MINISTER OF STAT E IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS  
(SHRI MULLAPPALLY RAMACHANDRAN): (a) and (b) Prior to the meeting of 
the Economic Intelligence Council (EIC) in January, 2010, a need was 
expressed for a mechanism to track, collate and analyze inward foreign 
remittances. Subsequently, a sub -committee was constituted within the 
Central Economic Intelligence Bureau (CEIB), which comprised 
representatives from Intelligence Bureau (IB), Enforcement Directorate 
(ED), Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) , Reserve Bank of India (RBI) 
and Central Economic Intelligence Bureau (CEIB). The Subgroup had 
recommended that IB share a negative list with FIU for further 
dissemination with reporting entities to track foreign remittances to 
organizations/individuals. 77 NGOs have come to adverse notice on a 
prima facie basis so far. 

 152 
(c) No Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA) contravention has so 
far been noticed by the Enforcement Directorate against any NGOs. 
(d) Government will continue to see that the joint mechanism takes 
up the closer monitoring, so that each individual case is taken to its 
logical conclusion in a timely manner as per provisions of law. 

 153

Outbreak of violent incidents in Jammu and Kashmir 
1624. DR. JANARDHAN WAGHMARE: Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Union Government is aware of the outbreak of 
violent incidents in Jammu and Kashmir in the past few months; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) the number of civilians, security personnel killed and injured 
and compensation paid to the affected persons; and 
(d) the steps taken by Government to identify and neutralize the 
elements responsible for fomenting such violence in the State? 
 THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS  
(SHRI AJAY MAKEN): (a) to (c) Yes, Sir. The law and order situation in 
the State of Jammu and Kashmir was near normal till May, 2010. 
However, beginning June 11, 2010, t he situation took a serious turn 
and a cycle of violence engulfed the Valley threatening law and order 
and public peace. Till date, 101 civilians and a police person have 
been killed in various actions by SFs in tackling violent mob. Besides 
557 civilians, 3429 personnel of JKP/CRPF have sustained injuries 
during the above protests. As on 2.10.2010, the State Government has 
sanctioned ex-gratia relief of Rs. 5 lakhs to the Next -of-Kin of 102 
persons killed in the civil disturbances since June 11, 2010. 
 (d) Law and Order is a State subject. Central Government have 
supported the Government of Jammu and Kashmir by deployment of 
additional Central Para- Military Forces to tackle law and order 
situation from time to time. The Central and State Governments made 

 163 
several appeals for dialogue and peace to resolve the situation. The 
Home Minister made a Statement in the Parliament on 04.08.2010. 
Further, the Prime Minister, met the All Party Delegation from the 
State on 10.08.2010 and appealed for peace, dialogue and 
reconciliation.  

 164 
The Prime Minister also convened an All Party Meeting on Jammu and 
Kashmir on  
15th September, 2010 and sought the guidance of various political 
parties represented in Parliament on the complex issues facing the 
State. In the light of the decision taken at the meeting, an All 
Parties Delegation visited Jammu and Kashmir on 21st and 22nd 
September, 2010 and met all sections of the people following which an 
8-point package was announced by the Government. 
 The State Government has been taking adequate measures to 
effectively handle the law and order situation in the State.

Protection to employees in informal sector 
 1646. SHRI MOINUL HASSAN: Will the Minister of LABOUR AND 
EMPLOYMENT be pleased to state: 
 (a) whether the ‘informal economy’ employs about 94 per cent of 
the total workforce, as per the NSS data; 
 (b) if so, the details thereof; 
 (c) whether the existing labour laws provide support and 
protection to the sector; 
 (d) if so, the details thereof; 
 (e) if not, whether Government plans of amending existing laws to 
ensure support and protection to those employed in the informal 
sector; 
 (f) whether Government proposes to introduce the Unorganized 
Sector Workers’ Social Security Bill; and 
 (g) if so, the details thereof? 
 THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
(SHRI HARISH RAWAT): (a) and (b) According to the survey conducted by 
the National Sample Survey Organization (NSSO) in 2004 -05, the total 
employment in both organized and the unorganized sectors in the 
country was 45.9 crore of these workers, 43.3 crore (about 94%) were 
in the unorganized sector. 
 (c) to (e) The Government has initiated several measures for the 
protection of the labourers in the unorganized sector. Various labour 
laws like the Minimum Wages Act, 1948; the Workmen Compensation Act, 
1923; the Equal Remuneration Act, 1976; the Buil ding and other 
Construction Workers (Regulation of Employment and Condition of 
Service) Act, 1996, Contract Labour (Abolition and Prohibition) Act, 
1970, Inter -State Migrant Workmen (Regulation of Employment and 
Conditions of Service) Act, 1979 etc. are ap plicable to the labourers 
in the unorganized sector also. The Government has set up Welfare 
Funds to provide social security/welfare measures of certain 
categories of workers i.e. beedi workers, certain non - 
coal mine workers and cine workers. The welfare measures include 
health care, housing, educational assistance for children, drinking 
water supply, etc. The labour laws are reviewed from time to time and 
amendment, as and when required, are made to meet the requirement of 
target group. 

 208 
 (f) and (g) Recognizing the need to providing social security, the 
Government has enacted the Unorganized Workers’ Social Security Act, 
2008. The salient features of the Unorganized Workers’ Social Security 
Act, 2008 are as under:— 
 • The Unorganized Workers’ Social Security Act, 2008 has since 
been enacted. The Act came into force w.e.f. 16.5.2009. 
Central Rules under the Act have been framed. 
 • Formulation of schemes by the Central Government for different 
sections of  

 209 
unorganized workers on matters relating to (a) life and 
disability cover;  
(b) health and maternity benefits; (c) old age protection (d) 
any other benefit as may be determined by the Central 
Government. 
 • Formulation of schemes relating to provident fund, employment 
injury benefits, housing, educational schemes for children, 
skill upgradation, funeral assistance and old age homes by the 
State Governments. 
 • Funding of the schemes to be specified in the scheme itself. 
 • Constitution of National Social Security Board under the 
chairmanship of Union Minister for Labour and Employment with 
Members of Parliament, unorganized workers, employers of 
unorganized workers, civil society, Central Ministries and 
State Governments. 
 • Adequate representation to persons belonging to the Scheduled 
Castes, the Scheduled Tribes, the Minorities and Women.

Steps to revive dying traditional weaving art 
 1696. SHRI ANIL M ADHAV DAVE: Will the Minister of TEXTILES be 
pleased to state the efforts made by Government to revive the dying 
traditional weaving art for textiles across the country? 
 THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF TEXTILES  
(SHRIMATI PANABAKA LAKSHMI): Sir the Government of India is determined 
and committed for the revival of the dying traditional weaving art for 
the textiles across the country. For revival of the handloom industry 
and to popularize the products in the national and international 
market following steps are taken by the Government of India:— 
 (a) Registration of Handloom items under the Geographical 
Indications of Goods (Registration and Protection) Act, 1999: 
  The Geographical Indications of Goods (Registration and 
Protection) Act, 1999 provid es legal protection to only such 
authorized users who have exclusive rights to produce the 
goods in respect of which it has been registered. Under this 
Act, measures are taken for protection of traditional handloom 
items e.g. Banarasi brocade, Jamdani of Bengal etc. It is 
proposed to cover about  
110 traditional handloom products of various States during the 
Eleventh Plan period @ Rs. 1.50 lakh per product. So far 
following handloom items have been registered under the GI 
Act:— 
  • Chanderi Sarees (Madhya P radesh) and Pochampally Sarees 
(Andhra Pradesh), Kotpad Handloom fabric, Kota Doria 
(Rajasthan), Solapur Chaddar, Solapur Terry towel 
(Maharashtra); have already been registered under the said 
Act; 
  • Narayanpet, Siddipet Gollabama, Mangalagiri and 
Venkatagiri Sarees of Andhra Pradesh; 
  • Sambalpuri Tie and Dye, Nuapatna Tie and Dye, Habaspuri 
Design, Bomkai Design, Posapally design, Khandua Nuapatna, 
Berhampur Kumbha Sarees (silk), Dhalapathar Temple Design 

 300 
fabrics of Orissa; 
  • Santipuri, Tangail, Tang ail Jamdani, Dhaniakhali, 
Baluchari, Korial, Garad Saree and Muslin of West Bengal; 
  • Silk Patola Sarees — single Ikat and Wollen acrylic shawl—
Kutch/Masharoo of Gujarat; Guledgud Khana, Udupi Saree of 
Karnataka; 
  • Banarasi Saree and Banarasi Brocades of Uttar Pradesh; 

 301 
  • Maheshwari handloom items of Madhya Pradesh; 
  • Kasargod, Kuthampully, Chendamangalam, Balaramapuram 
sarees and Kannur handloom furnishings of Kerala; 
  • Wangkhei Phee, Safi Lanphee/Sami Lamphee, Moirang Phee of 
Manipur  
State. 
  • In addition to the above Tamil Nadu State  registered 
Kancheepuram silk saree, Bhavani Jamukalam, Madurai 
Sungudi Sarees and action to register (1) Kovai cotton 
sarees (2) Salem silk and (3) Arani silk sarees of Tamil 
Nadu is under process. 
 (b) Promotion of use of HANDLOOM MARK: 
  The Handloom sector faces many challenges and with the 
technological developments, the handloom products are being 
increasingly replicated on powerlooms at a much lower cost. 
While the Government’s endeavor is to create condition s for 
the harmonious growth of the entire textile industry, at the 
same time it would also like to ensure that there is well 
defined and delineated areas for handlooms which is not unduly 
encroached by the powerlooms and mills. Hence, the “Handloom 
Mark” has been introduced to provide a collective identity to 
the handloom products which serves as a guarantee for the 
buyer that the product  
being purchased is genuinely hand woven and provides a 
distinct identity to the handloom products, both in India and 
abroad. The Handloom Mark has been registered under the Trade 
Marks Act, 1999 as well as for Copyright under the Copyright 
Act, 1957. 
  7420 Individual weavers, master weavers, handloom cooperative 
societies, handloom corporations, retailers and exporters, 
Self Help Groups, Joint Liability Groups, Consortia, Producer 
Company, Handloom Weavers Groups or any other legal entity, 
organization involved in Handloom activities and approved by 
the Development Commission for Handlooms are using the 
Handloom Mark labels with a one time registration fee. 
  745 retail outlets are selling the products with Handloom Mark 
label and 175.73 lakh handloom mark labels have been sold 
since 2006. 

 302 
 (c) Implementation of the Handloom (Reservation of Articles for 
Production) Act,  
1985:— 
  With a view to protect the interests and livelihood of the 
handloom weavers in the country, the Government of India 
promulgated the Handlooms (Reservation of Articles for 
Production) Act, 1985, dated 29.3.1985. Under the Act, 
protection to the handlooms sector was extended by way of 
reserving certain textile articles  
for exclusive production by handlooms. On the recommendation 
of the Advisory 

 303 
 Committee, 11 articles were reserved exclusive production by 
handlooms vide Notification No. 2160(E) dated  3.9.2008. The 
items reserved are:— 
  i. Saree; 
  ii. Dhoti; 
  iii Towel, Gamcha and Angavastram; 
  iv. Lungi; 
  v. Khes, Bedsheet, Bedcover, Counterpane, Furnishing (Incl. 
tapestry, upholstery); 
  vi. Jamakkalam Durry or Durret; 
  vii. Dress Material; 
  viii. Barrack Blankets, Kambal or Kamblies; 
  ix. Shawls, Loi, Muffler, Pankhi etc.; 
  x. Woollen Tweed; 
  xi. Chadar, Mekhala/Phanek. 
  The Office of the Development Commissioner for Handlooms 
implements the Act; Weavers Service Centres and Officers of 
the State Directors in charge of Handlooms implement the Act. 
During the Eleventh Plan period upto October, 2010, 8,37,151 
powerloom inspections have been conducted. 
 (d) Sant Kabeer Awards: 
  In order to give accreditation to the talented weavers and 
craft p ersons, the Government of India has introduced Sant 
Kabeer Awards w.e.f. the year 2009, under which one mounted 
gold coin, one shawl and a citation is given to each Awardee, 
which may number upto 10 in a year. In addition, financial 
assistance to the exten t of Rs. 6.00 lakh will also be given 
to each of the Sant Kabeer Awardee to innovate and create 10 
new products of high level of excellence of high asthenic 
value and high quality. 
 (e) Organising Design Exhibitions-cum-Dyeing Workshops: 
  The Weavers Serv ice Centres of this office organise Design 
Exhibitions-cum-Dyeing Workshops so as to educate the weavers 
and allied workers to improve their skills and to meet the 
market challenges by way of weaving new designs with different 
colour combinations. During the Eleventh Plan upto October, 

 304 
2010, 741 Design Exhibitions- cum-Dyeing Workshops have been 
organized. 
 (f) Providing new designs through National Centre for Textile 
Design: 
  The National Centre for Textile Design provides ethnic and 
contemporary designs developed by the Weavers’ Service Centres 
to the textile sector through the web  

 305 
portal www.designdiary.nic.in through the design pool 
available in 12 Indian  
regional languages, including Tamil. There are 1081 designs 
available on the website which are downloadable free of cost. 
More than one lakh viewers have visited this site. 
 (g) Apart from the above, to protect the handloom weavers and 
their traditional art, the Government of India is implementing 
following Schemes for the development of handloom sect or and 
welfare of weavers: 
  • Integrated Handlooms Development Scheme

“Clusters” of

support through design development and marketing linkages
